newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU pact accord possible at EU summit - Stark.
newsitem.headline: EMU pact accord possible at EU summit - Stark.

text.p: Juergen Stark, state sectretary at Germany's finance ministry, said on Monday he expected the main elements of a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline in European monetary union to be agreed by the December 13 Dublin EU summit.

Stark told a briefing in Brussels that some elements of the pact still had to be resolved. He said Germany, which has taken a hard line on the pact issue, was open to concrete proposals which could bring agreement.
"Agreement on the main elements of the stability pact is achievable by Dublin," Stark said.
But he added that certain technical details would not be agreed by then.
Under the terms of the planned stability pact, nations which exceed certain targets with their budget deficits will face sanctions and then fines if corrective action is not taken.

Stark left open the question of whether European Union officials would have agreed a definition of exceptional economic circumstances which would allow a country to exceed the target due to recessionary conditions.

Germany has insisted that a numerical definition must be set of what constitutes a bad recession, fearing that countries will otherwise be able to argue that weak economic conditions caused their budgetary excesses.

Germany has suggested that an exceptional situation is a contraction in the economy of two percent within a year. Another proposal suggests that a range of 0.5 percent to two percent contraction should be set as a possible exceptional range.
Asked to comment on this latter proposal, made by monetary committee chairman Nigel Wicks, Stark said, "We have clear ideas. The clearer the formulation, the better."
But he added, "We are open to constructive suggestions."
Asked about differences between the French and German delegations with regard to the stability pact, Stark told reporters, "We are doing our best to speak the same language as the French."
